claims.statement: The open-calls pull is a fixed, non-agent pipeline: for each funder it chooses a page (pinned URL, else the page the pull last read a call from, else candidate discovery plus a model pick), reads it through check_url and guarded_client, extracts calls with one structured model call, and writes only calls whose deadline is today or later (Asia/Kolkata); undated and past-deadline calls are only reported.

Page discovery builds candidates from pages Import already cited for the funder, its website, and one Tavily search restricted to the funder's own domain, keeps only candidates on the funder's own host, and the model's pick is discarded unless it is one of the given candidates; a missing TAVILY_API_KEY or failed search is reported rather than fatal.

read_page refuses URLs failing check_url (robots.txt and the source registry), PDFs and pages with under 200 characters of extracted text, and parses a pinned feed as RSS items into plain lines; extraction truncates pages to 30,000 characters and drops titles under four characters.

Calls are written via writer_funder.write_rfp, which dedupes on (funder_id, title, deadline) and records provenance and extractor_version 'calls-v1'; write_rfp attaches the first place and primary theme, extra places go to rfp_locations and extra themes to rfp_tags as secondary inferred tags, and the call's domains are added as tags so a call without a theme still reaches orgs in its field.

pull.run excludes hidden funders, reports pinned slugs not in Sangam as needing a look (the pull never creates a funder), runs funders with PARALLEL=4 concurrency pinned first, isolates each funder's failure as a report line, then closes expired open calls and runs flag_matches; close_expired uses the database current_date while the pull and matching use the Indian date.

A re-run reuses as a starting page only source_url from the newest rfps row whose extractor_version is the pull's own 'calls-v1', so a call written by Scout's research (naming a report) is never reused; the feed's last_pulled is likewise the newest fetched_at among 'calls-%' rows.

Funders land under 'NEEDS A LOOK' when there is no website or cited page, no candidate looks like a calls page, the page cannot be read (blocked, HTTP error, PDF, too little text), the funder is pinned but absent from Sangam, or any exception occurs; pinned.json keeps a per-source note that is appended to the failure so known dead ends are not rediscovered, and every pinned source recorded a dead end.

The UNDP procurement-notices feed is pinned as a feed but registered in rfps.json as crawl_only_with_permission, so check_url (ingest/reading/access.py) refuses it and it appears under 'NEEDS A LOOK'; feed-reading code exists in case permission is granted.

make calls-pull runs python -m app.ingest.calls.run: FUNDER=<slug> pulls one funder, CONFIRM=1 pulls every funder, and with neither it prints a warning and exits with status 2; make calls-match runs only flag_matches with no model call.

flag_matches inserts an rfp_matches row (matched_by 'rules:domain', week_of = Monday of the current week) for every organisation with members and every open, not-yet-expired call that shares a domain, rolling org tags (including programme tags) and call tags up through tags.parent_id to domain-kind tags; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means a re-run never changes an existing status, and orgs with members but no domain are counted as orgs_without_theme.

Migration 0049 only replaces rfp_matches_status_check so status may be flagged, saved, reviewed or dismissed (the base schema lacked saved); 'Not for us' remains dismissed, and week_of comes from the earlier 0010 migration.

rfp_matches is protected by RLS: rows are readable by the org's people and staff and updatable only by members/admins of the org (writable orgs) and staff, with UPDATE the only write grant for authenticated callers, so matches are inserted up front by the pull and stewards can only read.

GET /rfps/feed runs as the caller under RLS and returns org_id, org_slug, org_name, can_act, domains, last_pulled and items; the org query parameter is optional and defaults to the caller's first organisation by name; an item is included if it is saved regardless of the call's fate, or if it is not dismissed and the call is open with a deadline of today or later; an unknown org (or a caller with no organisation) is 404 and another org's feed comes back empty.

PATCH /rfps/{rfp_id}/matches/{org_id} accepts status flagged, saved, reviewed or dismissed (other values are 422) and optional match_notes (kept when omitted), records the caller's user id as matched_by, and returns 404 when no updatable row exists for the pair; test_rfps.py covers the happy path, unknown pair and bad status with the repository stubbed.

RfpWatchView loads one feed per selected organisation and buckets it client-side into For you, Closing soon (30 days) and Saved; CallCard flags 14 days or fewer as urgent, offers Save (saved/flagged toggle), Not for us (dismissed) and Ask about this call, shows a read-only line when can_act is false, and links only to http(s) URLs via safeHref because URLs were model-extracted.

Scout runs the pull through run_import_now(sources='funder_calls') handled by _calls_pull: staff_only runs first, names are resolved case-insensitively by name or slug (unknown names become report lines, none resolving returns a nothing-read message, empty means every funder), other source keys are reported as not run, pull.run's report is returned, and exceptions come back as a 'run_import_now failed' string rather than raising; no new tool, subagent or interrupt was added and the approval card replaces CONFIRM.

The Scout frontend exposes the pull as a staff-only 'Check open calls' task with its own 'Check open calls?' approval card showing the funders and a per-funder cost line, and labels the step 'Open calls · <funders>'.

RFP Watch milestones M1 (#228), M2 (#231), M3 (#232) and M4 (#246) have shipped, but the changelog's Not finished table still lists the staging exit gates and the design-system sync of the Ask page as left (even though a separate #311 entry says the UI kit recreates RFP Watch).

The extract prompt restricts calls to real invitations to apply (excluding procurement tenders, jobs, programme descriptions and always-open forms), asks for at most three themes, rupee bands only and only what the page states, and keeps a passed deadline so the pull can report it; the pick prompt returns null when no candidate looks like a calls page.

Test coverage of RFP Watch: test_cov_pipeline_calls.py tests the calls pull with fakes; test_cov_repositories.py tests flag_matches, feed, update_match and _themes against a database; test_rfps.py covers the PATCH route plus list_rfps paging parameters via recording_pool; test_cov_routes_members_rfps.py covers the list, feed, detail and matches routes with the repository stubbed; test_paging.py covers fetch_page and that list_rfps sorts on a unique id; test_cov_ingest_tools_pipeline.py covers _calls_pull with pull.run stubbed; RfpWatchView.test.tsx covers the screen. No test drives the feed over HTTP against a real database, and tests/evals/test_import_calls.py is about the Import eval harness's tool-call budgets, not this pipeline.

GET /rfps pages through repositories/paging.fetch_page, which requires SQL selecting COUNT(*) OVER () AS total and ending in an ORDER BY whose last key is id (raising ValueError before querying otherwise), appends LIMIT/OFFSET, and runs a separate count when a page past the end is empty so total stays correct; list_rfps orders by deadline (nulls last) then id, while GET /rfps/feed is unpaged.

The RFP Watch frontend calls getFeed and setStatus through call() in lib/api/rest.ts, which attaches authHeaders() and throws an ApiError carrying the response's detail; when Supabase keys are absent, lib/supabase/middleware.ts passes requests through ungated, so the feed has no session token unless DEV_LOGIN supplies a dev bearer.
